papers_read.title_as_printed: Cross-lingual detection of mild cognitive impairment based on temporal parameters of spontaneous speech (Gosztolya et al., Computer Speech & Language 69 (2021) 101215)

Linguistic-based Mild Cognitive Impairment detection using Informative Loss (Pourramezan Fard, Mahoor, Alsuhaibani, Dodge; Computers in Biology and Medicine 176 (2024) 108606). The record's claim_b still names P-11, a duplicate of P-6 (paper_b repointed P-11 -> P-6 on 2026-08-29); the 85.16% figure is P-6's.

what_each_reports.P-58: SVM on 15 ASR-derived temporal speech parameters from a telephone monologue; 33 English (New York; 19 HC, 14 MCI) and 33 Hungarian (Szeged; 20 HC, 13 MCI) speakers, speaker-wise LOO CV with nested tuning. All features monolingual: English accuracy 84.8%, AUC 0.932; Hungarian accuracy 75.8%, AUC 0.727; subsets and cross-lingual runs span '67-92%'.
what_each_reports.P-6: Transformer + InfoLoss on I-CONECT interview transcripts, 68 participants aged 75+ (34 MCI, 34 NC), subject-level 5-fold CV: accuracy 85.16%, AUC 84.75%; mean AUC 79.94% over five repeated fold configurations.

quantity_a: LOO-CV MCI vs HC classification scores from acoustic temporal/pause parameters of spontaneous telephone speech in two 33-person clinic samples (English, Hungarian).
quantity_b: 5-fold CV MCI vs NC accuracy/AUC from transcript semantics of semi-structured video conversations in the 68-person I-CONECT sample.
incompatible_if_same: No. 85.16% lies inside P-58's 67-92% range and matches P-58's English all-features accuracy (84.8%).

gates.task: match: MCI vs normal cognition detection (T1).
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: New York/Szeged clinic samples vs I-CONECT; the record's 'Yes' is wrong; no waiver.
gates.modality_family: match at family level (speech); different channels (acoustic pauses vs transcript semantics).

endpoint_and_metric: compatible metric types; P-58's '67-92%' is a multi-metric, multi-subset range rather than one estimate.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: no contested figure is at or above 0.97.
independence: Distinct studies and cohorts. This record duplicates C-71 (same two papers, same claims) after the P-11 -> P-6 deduplication.
grounds: The figure attributed to P-11 is P-6's 85.16% accuracy, which falls inside P-58's reported 67-92% range and matches P-58's English all-features accuracy (84.8%), so there is no disagreement.
P-58's '67-92%' spans several metrics, feature subsets, languages and ASR systems and cannot be set against a single accuracy.
The record is a duplicate of C-71 on the same pair (P-58 x P-6) since the 2026-08-29 repoint of paper_b from P-11 to P-6.

evidence_quotes.quote: because we got quite similar scores (67-92%) as we did in the monolingual cases (67-92% as well).
Besides an accuracy score of 84.8%, the recall/sensitivity and speciﬁcity values were also around 85%.
the framework achieves an overall accuracy of 85.16% and an AUC of 84.75%, with the corresponding std of 5.76 and 5.97, respectively.
34 were identified with MCI, while 34 were diagnosed with NC conditions.

record_defects: claim_b still reads 'P-11: 85.16% Acc on T1' although paper_b was repointed to P-6 (P-11 is a duplicate of P-6); the record now duplicates C-71 and should be marked as such.
dataset_equal 'Yes' is wrong: the cohorts are different (New York/Szeged vs I-CONECT).
The rejection reason 'Metric type unclear: Unknown / Acc' is inaccurate: P-58 reports accuracy and AUC for every feature set.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these papers; the recorded figures agree. Its status should follow C-71 as a duplicate.
